\label{ch:ru-letters-shch-e}
\hlchaptermodality{93}

\section[e]{\ru{э} (e) — the e that opens \ru{этот}}

\label{lesson:RU-W93-e}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: write \ru{я} and \ru{ё} once each, and name them.

Now say \textbf{\ru{этот}} (\emph{étot}), \textquotedblleft{}this\textquotedblright{}. You have read it for a long time. This lesson takes one letter out of it and puts it in your hand.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Script you'll notice: \ru{э}}
\textbf{\ru{э}} — \emph{e}.

It opens \textbf{\ru{этот}} (\emph{étot}), \textquotedblleft{}this\textquotedblright{}, and \textbf{\ru{эта}}. It looks like a \textbf{\ru{с}} turned to face the other way, with a short bar across the middle. It is the plain \emph{e} sound, with no \emph{y} in front of it, which is why it is mostly found at the start of a word.

\subsection*{Writing: \ru{э}}
\hlblockfigure{\detokenize{figures/RU-W93-e-filmstrip.pdf}}{How \ru{э} is written, stroke by stroke}

Put your pen on \ru{э} and follow its line. Copy the shape you can see — slowly, and larger than it is printed.

\begin{quote}
This book does not yet tell you \textbf{where to start this letter or which way to travel}. It is not written down here until it can be written down with a source. Copying what is in front of you needs no such source, and it is how the shape gets into your hand in the meantime.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Look:} at \textbf{\ru{этот}} and point at \ru{э} inside it
  \item \emph{Trace it:} \ru{э} three times, saying \emph{e} as you finish each one
  \item \emph{Write it:} \ru{ё}, then \ru{э}, from memory
  \item \emph{Read it:} \textbf{\ru{этот}} aloud once more
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
Which letter is this — \ru{э}? (\textbf{e}, \emph{e}.) Which word did it come from? (\textbf{\ru{этот}}, \emph{étot}, \textquotedblleft{}this\textquotedblright{}.)
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[shcha]{\ru{щ} (shcha) — the shch inside \ru{площадь}}

\label{lesson:RU-W93-shcha}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: write \ru{ё} and \ru{э} once each, and name them.

Now say \textbf{\ru{площадь}} (\emph{plóshchad}), \textquotedblleft{}a square\textquotedblright{}. You have read it for a long time. This lesson takes one letter out of it and puts it in your hand.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Script you'll notice: \ru{щ}}
\textbf{\ru{щ}} — \emph{shch}.

It is inside \textbf{\ru{площадь}} (\emph{plóshchad}), \textquotedblleft{}a square\textquotedblright{}. It is \textbf{\ru{ш}} with a small tail at the bottom right, and it sounds like a long, soft \emph{sh}.

\subsection*{Writing: \ru{щ}}
\hlblockfigure{\detokenize{figures/RU-W93-shcha-filmstrip.pdf}}{How \ru{щ} is written, stroke by stroke}

Put your pen on \ru{щ} and follow its line. Copy the shape you can see — slowly, and larger than it is printed.

\begin{quote}
This book does not yet tell you \textbf{where to start this letter or which way to travel}. It is not written down here until it can be written down with a source. Copying what is in front of you needs no such source, and it is how the shape gets into your hand in the meantime.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Look:} at \textbf{\ru{площадь}} and point at \ru{щ} inside it
  \item \emph{Trace it:} \ru{щ} three times, saying \emph{shch} as you finish each one
  \item \emph{Write it:} \ru{э}, then \ru{щ}, from memory
  \item \emph{Read it:} \textbf{\ru{площадь}} aloud once more
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
Which letter is this — \ru{щ}? (\textbf{shcha}, \emph{shch}.) Which word did it come from? (\textbf{\ru{площадь}}, \emph{plóshchad}, \textquotedblleft{}a square\textquotedblright{}.)
\end{tcolorbox}
